papers.title_in_file: Quantum Machine Learning for Cybersecurity: A Taxonomy and Future Directions
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, applications survey (selected), Limitations (Section VIII), Future Work
papers.what_it_is: A survey of quantum machine learning methods applied to cybersecurity tasks.

assertions.value: The authors state that QML testing in cybersecurity has largely been based on controlled evaluations, using static pre-processed datasets and simulated settings rather than live network environments.
quotes: The testing for QML in cybersecurity has largely been based on controlled evaluations.
the majority of existing works have used static, pre-processed datasets and simulated settings rather than live network environments.
assertions.certainty_reason: Survey's own characterization of the literature; no count given.

assertions.value: The authors state that current NISQ machines have limited qubits, are highly susceptible to noise and have short coherence times, which undermines threat detection reliability.
quotes: Current machines have limited qubits,
are highly susceptible to noise, and have short coherence times.
assertions.certainty_reason: Survey statement about hardware, no study behind it.

assertions.value: The authors report, citing Noah et al., that a hybrid QNN-based intrusion detection system achieved 96.8% accuracy against 92.3% for classical approaches.
assertions.anchor: Section IV, survey of Noah et al.
quotes: achieved 96.8% accuracy, whereas the classical approaches scored only achieved only 92.3%
assertions.certainty_reason: Result attributed to another study, in simulation as the survey describes.
assertions.reader_inference: Survey does not give dataset or baseline details here.

papers.title_in_file: The Impact of Feature Embedding Placement in the Ansatz of a Quantum Kernel in QSVMs
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study comparing data-first, data-last and a new data-weaved architecture for quantum embedding kernels.

assertions.value: The authors report that they categorize architectural patterns in quantum embedding kernels and show that existing architectural styles do not behave as the literature supposes.
quotes: We study and categorize various architectural patterns in QEKs and show that existing architectural styles do not behave as the literature supposes.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulation study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the data-weaved model achieves higher accuracies in almost all test cases with an equal number of parameterized gates.
quotes: Data-weaved model achieves higher accuracies in almost all test cases, with an equal amount parameterized gates compared to the other two models.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation on four small datasets.
assertions.reader_inference: Four small tabular datasets in simulation limit generality.

assertions.value: The authors state that every trial used 5 qubits, a batch size of 5 and 5000 optimization iterations.
quotes: we use 5 qubits (wires), a batch size of 5, run 5000 optimization iterations
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's statement of its own experimental setup, Section IV.

assertions.value: The authors state that the study does not indicate anything new about the usefulness of quantum embedding kernels in general.
quotes: We should note that this study does not indicate anything new about the usefulness of QEKs in general
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own scope statement, Introduction.

papers.title_in_file: Provable Advantage in Quantum PAC Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, technical overview, preliminaries, Grover subroutine statements; proofs not checked line by line
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper proving a square-root sample complexity advantage for quantum PAC learning when the learner has oracle access to the circuit preparing the quantum sample and its inverse.

assertions.value: The paper proves a square root advantage, up to polylogarithmic factors, for quantum PAC learning over classical PAC learning, in a model where the learner can call the circuit that generates the quantum sample and its inverse.
quotes: there is a square root advantage (up to polylogarithmic factors) for quantum PAC learning over classical PAC learning in the full, general model.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1.1, p.2; the advantage holds only under the stronger oracle access defined in Section 2.
assertions.reader_inference: The advantage rests on oracle access to the concept circuit and its inverse, which a standard learner does not have.

assertions.value: The paper proves that the upper bound is essentially tight, up to polylogarithmic factors.
quotes: we show that this upper bound is essentially tight, up to polylogarithmic factors
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1.2, p.3.

assertions.value: The authors state that they assume access to the quantum circuit that generates the quantum sample, and that the inverse oracle seems necessary for Grover search, so it is unclear whether an advantage is possible without the inverse.
quotes: we assume that we have access to the quantum circuit that generates it
The inverse oracle seems necessary for Grover's search, and thus it is unclear if a quantum advantage is possible.
assertions.certainty_reason: Model definition in Section 2 and open-questions paragraph.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Circuit for Imputation of Missing Data
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, discussion of optimization, Conclusions; appendix not read in full
papers.what_it_is: A variational quantum circuit (QIC) that imputes the last missing bit of a binary string, with analytic optimal parameters for simple cases.

assertions.value: The authors state they construct variational quantum circuits with gates complexity O(N ) and O(N 2) that return the last missing bit of a binary string for a specific distribution.
quotes: We construct variational quantum circuits with gates complexity O(N ) and O(N 2) that return the last missing bit of a binary string for a specific distribution.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' construction; complexity is circuit gate count.

assertions.value: The authors report Hellinger distance values, in the order stated in the quote, even for randomly generated distributions.
quotes: reaching values of the Hellinger distance in the order of
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result on small synthetic distributions.

assertions.value: The authors report that Bayesian optimization was compromised by barren plateaus in their circuit, preventing them from successfully minimizing the cost function.
quotes: While we attempted to employ Bayesian optimization, its effectiveness was ultimately compromised by the plateaus, preventing us from successfully minimize the cost function.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own attempt reported in text; details in Appendix A.

papers.title_in_file: Towards Practical Quantum Neural Network Diagnostics with Neural Tangent Kernels
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Theory, Section III start, Conclusions; numerical Section IV skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A framework that uses the quantum neural tangent kernel at initialization to diagnose training speed, critical learning rate and inference of quantum neural networks.

assertions.value: The authors show how a critical learning rate and a characteristic decay time for the average training error can be estimated from the spectrum of the QNTK evaluated at the initialization stage.
quotes: we show how a critical learning rate and a characteristic decay time for the average training error can be estimated from the spectrum of the QNTK evaluated at the initialization stage.
assertions.certainty_reason: Derivation under lazy training plus simulations.

assertions.value: The authors report that QNTK diagnostics yields accurate approximations of QNN behavior for sufficiently deep circuits and can provide insights for shallow QNNs.
quotes: QNTK diagnostics yields accurate approximations of QNN behavior for sufficiently deep circuits, can provide insights for shallow QNNs
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulations on several architectures and datasets.

assertions.value: The authors state that most formal results are obtained under specific assumptions, the lazy training regime, which are typically difficult to realize in practice.
quotes: most of the formal results are obtained under specific assumptions, i.e., the so called lazy training regime, which are typically difficult to realize in practice.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' statement of scope, Introduction p.2.

assertions.value: The authors state that the QNTK might in practice only be useful as a rough estimate of the generalization properties of the model under study.
quotes: the QNTK might in practice only be useful as a rough estimate of the generalization properties of the model under study.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' stated limitation, Section V.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Equilibrium Propagation: Gradient-Descent Training of Quantum Systems
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that extends equilibrium propagation to quantum systems whose ground state minimizes the mean energy.

assertions.value: The author states that equilibrium propagation is extended to quantum systems, where the minimized energy function is the mean energy functional, whose minimum is the ground state of the Hamiltonian.
quotes: We extend EP to quantum systems, where the energy function that is minimized is the mean energy functional (expectation value of the Hamiltonian), whose minimum is the ground state of the Hamiltonian.
assertions.certainty_reason: Analytic derivation in the paper; not independently checked here.

assertions.value: The author states that simulating QEP numerically is the next step, so the paper reports no numerical results.
quotes: The next step would be to simulate QEP numerically.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 5, p.9; no experiments appear in the paper.

assertions.value: The author states that multiple measurements are often required to obtain accurate gradient estimates of the cost function in the quantum setting.
quotes: Multiple measurements are often required to obtain accurate gradient estimates of the cost function
assertions.certainty_reason: Author's statement; not quantified in the paper.

papers.title_in_file: Implementing a distance-based classifier with a quantum interference circuit
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, experiment and simulation results, appendix B start
papers.what_it_is: A minimal quantum interference circuit that realizes a distance-based classifier, demonstrated on the IBM Quantum Experience and in simulation on the Iris data.

assertions.value: The authors state that after state preparation the circuit consists only of a Hadamard gate and two single-qubit measurements, and computes the distance between data points in quantum parallel.
quotes: After state preparation, the circuit only consists of a Hadamard gate as well as two single-qubit measurements, and computes the distance between data points in quantum parallel.
assertions.certainty_reason: Circuit definition in the abstract and Fig. 3.

assertions.value: The authors report that simulation results closely resemble the theoretical predictions while the experimental results on the IBM device show substantial errors.
quotes: yield simulation results that closely resemble the theoretical predictions, while the experimental results show substantial errors.
assertions.certainty_reason: One small experiment on a five-qubit device.

assertions.value: The authors report that in simulation the classifier gives a 100% success rate for Iris classes 1 and 2 and for 1 and 3, and a 93% average success rate for classes 2 and 3.
quotes: the entire dataset for classes 1 and 2 as well as for 1 and 3 of Iris species results in a 100% success rate
distinguishing classes 2 and 3 only yield a 93% average success
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation on the Iris dataset with an 80/20 split.

assertions.value: The authors state that the logarithmic scaling holds if an efficient state preparation routine is known, and that the speedup is not necessarily based on quantum resources.
quotes: If an efficient state preparation routine is known, the algorithm explored here harvests the same logarithmic scaling
is not necessarily based on quantum resources
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own caveat in the Introduction.
